title: Political Ad Spending Expected to Hit Nearly $11 Billion in 2026

facts.fact: AdImpact projects that candidates, campaigns, committees and outside groups will spend $10.8 billion on advertising in the 2026 election cycle.
facts.quote: candidates, campaigns, committees and outside groups will drop a staggering $10.8 billion on advertising during the 2026 election cycle

facts.fact: According to AdImpact, the projected $10.8 billion for 2026 would be a more-than-20-percent increase over the $8.9 billion spent in 2022, making it the most expensive non-presidential cycle in history.
facts.quote: marking a more-than-20-percent increase over the $8.9 billion spent in 2022, according to AdImpact’s report.

facts.fact: Political advertising spending in 2024 was $11.2 billion, with about $3.2 billion of that targeting the presidential race.
facts.quote: In 2024, $11.2 billion was spent on political advertising, with about $3.2 billion of that targeting the presidential race specifically.

facts.fact: AdImpact predicts $1.1 billion in political ad spending in California in 2026.
facts.quote: AdImpact predicting $1.1 billion in spending in the Golden State.

facts.fact: AdImpact projects nearly $1 billion will be spent on advertising in Michigan.
facts.quote: AdImpact’s report projects that nearly $1 billion will be spent on advertising in Michigan

facts.fact: AdImpact expects Texas, Georgia and North Carolina to each garner upwards of $550 million in ad spending.
facts.quote: states like Texas, Georgia and North Carolina are expected to garner upwards of $550 million in ad spending

facts.fact: AdImpact projects CTV's share of political ad spending will rise to 23 percent in 2026, a 2-percentage-point increase over 2024 levels, reaching nearly $2.5 billion.
facts.quote: CTV’s spending share will increase to 23 percent next year – a 2 percent increase over 2024 levels – to nearly $2.5 billion

facts.fact: AdImpact projects broadcast television's share will rise by 1 percent in 2026 but its overall revenue will fall by $97 million.
facts.quote: Broadcast television, meanwhile, is projected to increase by just 1 percent, but lose $97 million overall in revenue.

facts.fact: AdImpact projects local cable political ad spending will drop from $1.7 billion in 2022 to $1.29 billion in 2026.
facts.quote: spending on local cable dropping from $1.7 billion in 2022 to $1.29 billion in 2026

facts.fact: AdImpact expects radio and satellite to hold historic shares of 3 percent and 1 percent of political ad spending, respectively.
facts.quote: Radio and satellite spending are expected to hold onto their historic shares of 3 percent and 1 percent, respectively

facts.fact: AdImpact has logged around $900 million in political ad spending through August 26, 2025.
facts.quote: AdImpact has already logged around $900 million in spending through Aug. 26

facts.fact: At the same point in 2023, $657 million had been spent on political advertising.
facts.quote: $657 million had already been spent at the same point in 2023

facts.fact: By August 2021, $572 million had been spent on political advertising.
facts.quote: $572 million had been spent by August 2021

facts.fact: As of August 2025, congressional spending accounted for 18 percent of all political ad activity, compared with 5 percent at the same point in 2023.
facts.quote: congressional spending accounting for 18 percent of all political ad activity as of August

facts.fact: AdImpact expects ad spending on House races to reach $2.2 billion in 2026, a 27 percent increase over the 2024 cycle and a 40 percent increase over 2022.
facts.quote: Ad spending on House races is expected to hit $2.2 billion in 2026 – a 27 percent increase over the 2024 election cycle and a 40 percent increase over 2022 levels.

facts.fact: AdImpact projects Senate ad spending to slightly outpace 2024 levels, reaching $2.8 billion.
facts.quote: Senate ad spending is projected to slightly outpace 2024 levels, coming in at $2.8 billion

facts.fact: AdImpact projects $3.9 billion will be spent on downballot and state legislative contests, which it says will account for more than a third of total 2026 ad spending.
facts.quote: AdImpact is projecting that $3.9 billion will be dropped on these contests.
